picks.excerpt: At the Aspen Festival of Ideas talk 'Who Owns the Future of Hollywood,' Jodie Foster quipped that Apple's blockbuster 'F1' seemed like it could have been made by AI and written by a computer. She allowed that AI tools are useful for 'small helpful things' like previs, while questioning formula-driven studio filmmaking in the AI era.

Karlovy Vary's expanded Industry Days (July 5-8) puts 'demystifying AI' on the main stage: a hands-on presentation of currently available AI tools for film professionals, plus sessions on microdramas and other disruption threats, per KVIFF Film Industry Office head Hugo Rosak. The 60th edition frames AI literacy as a core skill for European film pros.

Neon released the trailer for Hirokazu Koreeda's Cannes-premiered sci-fi grief drama 'Sheep in the Box' (in US theaters July 24), in which a Japanese couple welcomes an AI-powered android re-creation of their deceased son into their home — Koreeda's plea for human imagination in the AI age.

Writer-director Paul Feig ('Bridesmaids') derided generative AI as 'an amalgamation of our old ideas,' arguing that the technology can only recombine what humans already made and coining 'HI — human intelligence' as the industry's real engine.
